correctness.rationale: The determinant identity follows from the complete Leibniz expansion for a chordless odd cycle: disjoint edge transpositions have order-independent terms and only the two directed complete cycles contribute order-dependent powers. Positive definiteness of the normalized symmetric Jacobi matrix makes det(sD-W) strictly increasing for s above the Perron root. The competing scalar term is strictly decreasing for lambda in (0,1), proving a unique root. The Gauss-Seidel sweep matrix is entrywise nonnegative and strictly contractive in the A-energy norm, so that root equals its spectral radius. Strict ordering by absolute ascent imbalance and the Eulerian optimizer census follow algebraically. Exact SymPy identities and rational brackets and exhaustive five- and seven-cycle supplemental sweeps were replayed from the specified standalone script; finite tests are not used as general proof. The result is restricted to odd simple cycles and asymptotic spectral radius.

originality.rationale: Varga 1959 proves the Jacobi-squared lower bound and consistency conditions, but not the strict ranking and precise rates of orders which fail to attain it on arbitrary weighted odd rings. His p-cyclic result addresses consistently ordered systems. Oswald and Zhou 2015 study randomized reorderings and inequalities, not exact order-by-order odd-cycle spectra. Searches for cyclic ascent imbalance and all-permutation Gauss-Seidel rates did not reveal a dominating exact classification. The Heller 1957 historical paper remains incompletely accessible, an explicit publication-priority risk, not a claim that it is irrelevant.
residual_risks: Original Heller (1957) complete paper was inaccessible; possible overlap with full characteristic-polynomial invariance cannot be excluded.
Bibliographic and indexed mathematical searches are not exhaustive; a previously published equivalent all-order odd-ring theorem may exist.
The claim concerns spectral radius and not fixed-horizon A-norms; extrapolating to transient convergence would exceed the proof.

value.rationale: Odd cycles are the minimal topological obstruction to bipartite/consistent red–black ordering. Classifying every rate and every fastest ordering under arbitrary diagonal and conductance heterogeneity gives a structural scheduling rule without requiring parameter knowledge, quantifies the strict penalty above the classical Jacobi-squared benchmark, and determines exactly how many orders attain the optimum. This goes beyond routine Jacobi estimates or a small finite census and can guide robust sequential solver ordering on ring-structured SPD systems.
